examples.title: Blink the built-in LED
examples.description: Turn the built-in D13 LED on and off. Learn the order of statements and milliseconds.

examples.title: Serial hello
examples.description: Print a short greeting repeatedly in Serial Monitor. Match the sketch and Monitor baud rates.

examples.title: Potentiometer values in Monitor
examples.description: Read a potentiometer on A0 and print its 0–1023 ADC value. Turn the knob to see the number change.

examples.title: Potentiometer dims a PWM LED
examples.description: Map an A0 potentiometer reading to PWM brightness for an LED. A PWM output is required for analogWrite.

examples.title: Button controls an LED
examples.description: Read a button and change an LED. The input needs the pull-up or wiring described in the blocks.

examples.title: Traffic lights
examples.description: Run a simple red/amber/green traffic-light sequence. Each wait makes the next visible phase last longer.

examples.title: DS18B20 thermometer + Plotter
examples.description: Request a DS18B20 conversion without waiting, read it after 800 ms, and show a thermometer dashboard after Plotter Start.

examples.title: 16×2 I2C LCD hello
examples.description: Show a greeting on a 16×2 HD44780 LCD with PCF8574 I2C backpack. Check address and contrast first.

examples.title: 16×2 LCD potentiometer
examples.description: Read a potentiometer and print the value on a 16×2 I2C LCD. Learn how repeated prints update a text display.

examples.title: SPI OLED uptime counter
examples.description: Count seconds on an SSD1306 SPI OLED using a named device and no framebuffer. Update with millis timing.

examples.title: ST7735 colour TFT text
examples.description: Print text and an analog reading on an ST7735 colour TFT over hardware SPI. Match the panel type and wiring.

examples.title: Find I2C device addresses
examples.description: Scan the I2C bus and print responding addresses in Monitor. Use it to discover the address of an attached module.

examples.title: 0.91-inch I2C OLED text
examples.description: Print text on a 128×32 SSD1306 I2C OLED. U8x8 sends character tiles without a full pixel framebuffer.

examples.title: Grove RGB LCD
examples.description: Use the text and RGB backlight of a Grove JHD1313 LCD. This module uses a different library from PCF8574 backpacks.

examples.title: Single piezo beep
examples.description: Make a passive piezo beep using the Arduino core tone function. This AVR engine uses Timer2 interrupts.

examples.title: Simple piezo melody
examples.description: Play a short tune with the basic core tone blocks. Compare this blocking lesson with the nonblocking named music examples.

examples.title: DS18B20 temperature on LCD
examples.description: Read a DS18B20 temperature and show it on an I2C character LCD. Check the sensor pull-up and LCD address.

examples.title: 20×4 LCD animation (legacy helper)
examples.description: Play a preset 20×4 LCD animation with an older helper. Example 28 exposes the animation as individual blocks.

examples.title: 20×4 LCD potentiometer
examples.description: Show a potentiometer reading on a 20×4 LCD. Use the named LCD and buffer examples for reusable display logic.

examples.title: Servo sweep (core timer library)
examples.description: Move a hobby servo between three angles with the core Servo library. Pulse edges are timer interrupt driven; the waits pause the main loop.

examples.title: 28BYJ stepper (blocking legacy lesson)
examples.description: Move a 28BYJ-48 through a ULN2003 using a blocking legacy helper. Example 30 provides named, accelerated, nonblocking control.
notes: Legacy lesson retained for existing projects. Prefer named-device examples 30, 62 or 70 for new work.

examples.title: DHT22 climate + Plotter
examples.description: Read DHT22 temperature and humidity every 2.1 seconds. Plotter Start opens separate temperature and humidity views; invalid readings are reported as text.

examples.title: HC-SR04 distance in Monitor
examples.description: Measure HC-SR04 echo duration and print distance. Sensor reads can block while waiting for an echo; leave at least 60 ms between readings.

examples.title: NeoPixel colour cycle
examples.description: Change WS2812 RGB LED colours. The strip library keeps a small colour buffer and sends it on show.

examples.title: NEC remote commands
examples.description: Read each NEC remote command once and print only valid frames. Poll promptly while IRremote uses Timer2 for reception.

examples.title: 74HC595 chasing LED
examples.description: Send a shifting one-bit pattern to a 74HC595 so one LED chases across eight outputs. Wiring is declared once.

examples.title: STEP/DIR stepping (legacy helper)
examples.description: Generate a simple STEP/DIR movement with a legacy helper. Use example 70 for fast hardware-timed continuous motion.
notes: Legacy lesson retained for existing projects. Prefer named-device examples 30, 62 or 70 for new work.

examples.title: 20×4 animation made from blocks
examples.description: Build a 20×4 moving-text animation from editable blocks rather than a preset animation helper.

examples.title: STEP/DIR acceleration (legacy helper)
examples.description: Request STEP/DIR positions and repeatedly call AccelStepper run to accelerate and decelerate. Older helper format retained for comparison.
notes: Legacy lesson retained for existing projects. Prefer named-device examples 30, 62 or 70 for new work.

examples.title: Named 28BYJ: accelerated back and forth
examples.description: Use one named 28BYJ-48 motor to travel between two positions with acceleration. Call run continuously; no delay interrupts the coil sequence.

examples.title: Setup, loop, function and variable
examples.description: Separate one-time setup from repeated loop work, create a variable, and call a reusable function.

examples.title: Math operations
examples.description: Try arithmetic, ranges and mathematical operations. Observe how connected value blocks form expressions.

examples.title: Array animation with millis timing
examples.description: Update array data on a millis schedule so loop can continue between animation steps.

examples.title: Local variables and 2D arrays
examples.description: Compare global and local declarations and address a two-dimensional array with zero-based indices.

examples.title: Named stepper: position targets
examples.description: Declare a STEP/DIR device once, request target positions and keep servicing the loop engine until each target is reached.

examples.title: Named 20×4 I2C LCD
examples.description: Declare a 20×4 I2C LCD once and print through its named actions without repeating address or dimensions.

examples.title: Servo and distance sensor sweep
examples.description: Sweep a servo and take HC-SR04 distance readings. Allow settling time and remember that an echo read briefly blocks.

examples.title: I2C EEPROM: values and text
examples.description: Write and read typed values and text in a 24LC256 I2C EEPROM. Addresses are byte offsets, separate from its I2C bus address.
notes: Writes a small EEPROM test area. Use a chip with no data you need to retain.

examples.title: SPI EEPROM: values and text
examples.description: Write and read typed values and text in a 25LC256 SPI EEPROM using one named chip-select configuration.
notes: Writes a small EEPROM test area. Use a chip with no data you need to retain.

examples.title: SPI Flash: erase, write, read
examples.description: Erase a W25Q32 Flash sector, write a value/text, then read it back. Flash cannot overwrite programmed bits without erase.
notes: Erases a whole 4 KB Flash sector before writing. Use a chip with no data you need to retain.

examples.title: SD text file
examples.description: Create or append a text file on an SPI SD card, then flush and close it. A FAT filesystem remains readable on a computer.

examples.title: SD BMP: coordinate pixels
examples.description: Create a small BMP file on SD and write pixels by coordinates. File storage replaces a full image array in RAM.

examples.title: Radar measurements → BMP
examples.description: Sweep a servo, measure distance, and draw results into an SD BMP. This combined sketch has little memory margin on ATmega168.
notes: Small remaining memory margin: 240 bytes Flash and 284 bytes SRAM before stack/heap. Keep this advanced; compile success does not measure stack or dynamic allocation.
Combined SD, sensing and motion: advanced, little stack/heap headroom on ATmega168. Compile size is not a runtime stack test.

examples.title: Stream monochrome BMP to SD
examples.description: Write a monochrome BMP in raster order, one pixel at a time, then finish the file. No full image buffer is allocated.

examples.title: Buzzer: nonblocking beep
examples.description: Start a nonblocking note on a named passive buzzer while the main loop remains available for other tasks.

examples.title: Three independent melody voices
examples.description: Play three independent melody voices on three passive buzzers. The optional IRQ mixer shares one Timer2 and consumes periodic CPU time.
notes: Three-voice IRQ music shares Timer2. Each passive buzzer uses a separate output; Timer2 is unavailable for another independent engine.

examples.title: Melody with rests
examples.description: Define a reusable flash melody with rests and play it through a named buzzer.

examples.title: SD text-note melody
examples.description: Read text notes from a known SD file and pass each note record to the buzzer. The line parser avoids loading the whole tune.
notes: Small remaining memory margin: 820 bytes Flash and 276 bytes SRAM before stack/heap. Keep this advanced; compile success does not measure stack or dynamic allocation.

examples.title: Polar scan → streamed BMP
examples.description: Convert a polar servo/distance scan into row-ordered BMP output on SD. Advanced example with tight AVR memory margins.
notes: Small remaining memory margin: 804 bytes Flash and 276 bytes SRAM before stack/heap. Keep this advanced; compile success does not measure stack or dynamic allocation.
Combined SD, sensing and motion: advanced, little stack/heap headroom on ATmega168. Compile size is not a runtime stack test.

examples.title: Multidimensional arrays and variable indices
examples.description: Use variables for every index of a multidimensional array. Fixed dimensions reserve RAM; indices choose an element at runtime.

examples.title: BMP grayscale levels
examples.description: Create a grayscale BMP with selected palette levels and append calculated shades. Values must fit the chosen output range.

examples.title: RGB BMP gradient
examples.description: Stream an RGB gradient into a BMP file without keeping the picture in AVR RAM.

examples.title: 1024-shade grayscale PGM
examples.description: Write a 1024-level grayscale PGM, preserving more than 8 bits per sample. Use a computer image viewer that supports PGM.

examples.title: High-depth RGB PPM
examples.description: Write a high-depth RGB PPM with selected per-channel range. This format preserves precision beyond an 8-bit BMP channel.

examples.title: Typed function arguments and results
examples.description: Define a function with typed float and uint32_t arguments and an explicit result type.

examples.title: Pack flags and bit fields
examples.description: Pack several flags and small fields into integers with masks, shifts and extraction blocks.

examples.title: AVR direct-port blink
examples.description: Blink D13 through AVR port registers. Compare the generated code and Flash use with ordinary digitalWrite.

examples.title: AVR input and pull-up
examples.description: Configure an AVR port input and pull-up with masks, then read its bit without changing neighbouring pins.

examples.title: Direct-port byte driver
examples.description: Drive a byte pattern through direct port operations. This advanced lesson exposes register ownership and bit masks.

examples.title: Read SPI Flash JEDEC ID
examples.description: Send the JEDEC-ID command to an SPI Flash chip and read its identification bytes using generic SPI blocks.

examples.title: I2C register read
examples.description: Write a register pointer and read data from an I2C device using generic transactions. Match the address/register to the attached chip.

examples.title: Interrupt counter with atomic snapshot
examples.description: Increment a volatile counter in an interrupt and copy it atomically before using it in loop.

examples.title: Bidirectional Serial echo
examples.description: Echo incoming Serial bytes back to Monitor. Test sending text and different line endings without a blocking String read.

examples.title: Plotter: automatic lines
examples.description: After Plotter Start, send two numeric CSV columns from A0. Automatic mode discovers two line traces without a JSON header.

examples.title: Plotter: potentiometer dashboard
examples.description: After Plotter Start, send one A0 value. A Flash-resident header asks the PC to calculate voltage and show lines, a gauge, a bar and raw values.

examples.title: External interrupt edge counter
examples.description: Count edges on external interrupt D2. A physical button may bounce and create several electrical edges per press.

examples.title: Pin-change counters
examples.description: Use pin-change interrupts on D4 and D5 to keep separate counters, then copy the values safely in loop.

examples.title: Timer1 periodic interrupt
examples.description: Use Timer1 for a periodic interrupt and keep the handler short. The timer is then unavailable to Servo, fast stepper and its PWM channels.

examples.title: Attach and detach interrupts
examples.description: Attach or detach a configured interrupt using Monitor commands while preserving the accumulated counter.

examples.title: Photocell scanner: image + chart
examples.description: After Plotter Start, scan a photocell with two hardware servos. Send one gray pixel and chart sample at a time; the computer retains the image.

examples.title: Continuous stepper: potentiometer ramp
examples.description: Use a potentiometer to set signed continuous stepper speed with acceleration. The software loop engine must still be serviced every pass.

examples.title: Servo pulse width in microseconds
examples.description: Map a potentiometer to servo pulse microseconds for finer command increments than whole degree values.

examples.title: LCD character buffer
examples.description: Prepare an 80-byte LCD character grid in RAM, then send the finished 20×4 frame once. Legacy text mode treats zero as a space.

examples.title: OLED packed pixel tile
examples.description: Build a 128-byte packed OLED tile: each byte stores eight vertical pixels. Send the tile without allocating a full-screen buffer.
notes: Uses a 128-byte tile. Do not allocate a 1024-byte OLED framebuffer on a board with 1024 bytes total SRAM.

examples.title: NeoPixel RGB buffer
examples.description: Prepare RGB values in an array, copy them to the NeoPixel library buffer and call show once for the finished frame.

examples.title: TFT RGB565 tile
examples.description: Prepare a small RGB565 colour tile and send it to an ST7735 TFT in one SPI transaction.

examples.title: A note read from a variable
examples.description: Pass a note record through a variable to the music parser. The same format can come from EEPROM, Serial or an SD line.

examples.title: Polyphonic SD score
examples.description: Play a timed, polyphonic score from SD without loading it all into RAM. Three IRQ voices and the SD cache leave a small stack margin.
notes: Small remaining memory margin: 842 bytes Flash and 196 bytes SRAM before stack/heap. Keep this advanced; compile success does not measure stack or dynamic allocation.
Three-voice IRQ music shares Timer2. Each passive buzzer uses a separate output; Timer2 is unavailable for another independent engine.

examples.title: Timer1 stepper: fine speed commands
examples.description: Start a Timer1 STEP/DIR motor stopped, then change signed target speed in small or large increments through Monitor. Hardware pulses and acceleration continue independently of loop.
notes: Small remaining memory margin: 832 bytes Flash and 388 bytes SRAM before stack/heap. Keep this advanced; compile success does not measure stack or dynamic allocation.

examples.title: Hardware Servo + hardware sound
examples.description: Use a potentiometer to control hardware Servo pulses on D9 while a hardware buzzer on D11 plays a melody. Timer1 and Timer2 have separate owners.

examples.title: LCD custom faces from a buffer
examples.description: Define a 5×8 face in LCD glyph slot 0, then animate two faces through an 80-byte raw-code buffer. Eight slots and variable indices are supported.

examples.title: Plotter: multiple instruments together
examples.description: Compare A0 with a generated triangle in overlaid lines, a multi-needle gauge, grouped bars, two XY traces and a raw table. Start/Stop controls one shared stream.

examples.title: Plotter: PC math and live configuration
examples.description: Send one voltage plus device time and let the PC calculate mean, RMS, limits, sum, derivative and integral. After five seconds, a live header changes the averaging window.

examples.title: Plotter: RGB painting, no extra hardware
examples.description: Paint an RGB gradient one pixel at a time while charts and bars show the colours. No external hardware or AVR image buffer is needed.
notes: All pixels are held on the computer. The Arduino sends one pixel and chart sample at a time.

examples.title: blink
examples.description: Original BlocklyDuino blink workspace retained for importing older projects.

examples.title: click color
examples.description: Original BlocklyDuino demonstration workspace retained as a legacy import, outside the current AVR168 compile audit.

examples.title: servo potentio
examples.description: Original potentiometer-to-servo workspace retained as a legacy import. Prefer the named servo lessons for new work.
